= Vert.x WebSocket
:artifactid: camel-vertx-websocket-starter

Receive and send WebSocket messages with Vert.x, as a WebSocket server or as a client of a remote WebSocket server.

== What's inside

* xref:{csb-camel-components}::vertx-websocket-component.adoc[Vert.x WebSocket component], URI syntax: `vertx-websocket:host:port/path`

Please refer to the above links for usage and configuration details.

== Maven coordinates

[source,xml]
----
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.camel.springboot</groupId>
    <artifactId>camel-vertx-websocket-starter</artifactId>
</dependency>
----

== Spring Boot Auto-Configuration

The starter supports 13 options, which are listed below.

[width="100%",cols="2,5,^1,2",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Description | Default | Type
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.allow-origin-header | Whether the producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true add an Origin header to the WebSocket handshake request, as the default for the endpoints of this component. See the allowOriginHeader endpoint option. | true | Boolean
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.autowired-enabled | Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc. | true | Boolean
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.bridge-error-handler | Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored. | false | Boolean
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.default-host | The host of an endpoint whose URI has no host, such as vertx-websocket:/chat. The default 0.0.0.0 makes the server consumer bind to all network interfaces. | 0.0.0.0 | String
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.default-port | The port of an endpoint whose URI has no port. With the default 0, the server consumer binds to a free port that the operating system picks, and the producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true connect to port 80, or to port 443 with TLS. | 0 | Integer
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.enabled | Whether to enable auto configuration of the vertx-websocket component. This is enabled by default. |  | Boolean
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.lazy-start-producer | Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing. | false | Boolean
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.origin-header-url | The value of the Origin header of the WebSocket handshake request, as the default for the endpoints of this component. See the originHeaderUrl endpoint option. |  | String
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.router | The Vert.x Router that the HTTP servers of the server consumers use, unless the router option of the endpoint is set. The one router serves the HTTP servers of all hosts and ports. If not set, the Router bean of the registry is used when there is exactly one, and otherwise each HTTP server gets a new router. The option is a io.vertx.ext.web.Router type. |  | Router
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.synchronous | Whether the consumers route each message synchronously, as the default for the endpoints of this component. See the synchronous endpoint option. | false | Boolean
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.use-global-ssl-context-parameters | Whether to use the global SSL context parameters of the CamelContext for each endpoint that the component creates and that has no sslContextParameters. See the sslContextParameters endpoint option. | false | Boolean
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.vertx | To use an existing Vert.x instance instead of creating a new one. If not set, the component uses the Vertx bean of the registry when there is exactly one, and otherwise creates its own instance, which it closes when it stops. The option is a io.vertx.core.Vertx type. |  | Vertx
| camel.component.vertx-websocket.vertx-options | The VertxOptions of the Vert.x instance that the component creates. Not used when the component uses an existing Vert.x instance, from the vertx option or a Vertx bean of the registry. The option is a io.vertx.core.VertxOptions type. |  | VertxOptions
